component: P16 local comparison capture, response validation and measurement reporting
constraints: Local trusted Python API inspection plus a separate Node primitive comparison; no service, device transport or target timing contract.
At most 64 KiB sent to one reviewed child; retained stdout at most 4 KiB and stderr counted/discarded above 4 KiB.
Report source identities, exact response types, raw Python batch intervals and tracing scope; reject missing comparison, optimized mode and visible source changes.
alternatives: Direct Python driver with asyncio subprocess callbacks and independent Node primitive probe.
Node child_process orchestration with maxBuffer and timeout controls.
Rust Tokio process/pipe orchestration with explicit output quotas and child cleanup.
Java/Kotlin Process orchestration with explicit stream consumption and destruction.
pyperf worker calibration or JVM JMH for a separately specified statistical benchmark.
rationale: KEEP the driver in the interpreter whose API objects and allocations are inspected. Another-language orchestrator still needs a Python execution boundary; it does not remove response typing, source or cleanup obligations.

The small private callback helper counts data before retaining it. High-level accumulating capture followed by a size check would not provide that retained-output bound. Existing real-child tests cover overflow, exit failure and timeout cleanup.

KEEP integer Python clock subtraction and explicit tracing ownership. Single batches describe diagnostic elapsed samples; pyperf/JMH address statistical benchmarking, which this tool explicitly does not claim.

Twenty focused methods pass. A live Python/Node run passes six primitive comparisons. Removing the final source-change check in memory causes five existing rejection assertions to fail. No new implementation defect demonstrated.
limits: Current alternatives are compared by official documented properties, not implemented end-to-end or ranked by speed.
Retained-output bounds are not total RSS or child CPU bounds. Creation precedes exchange timeout; cleanup has a separate cooperative timeout; descendants are not managed.
Node checks primitives and parser observations, not full passport semantics. Python and Node single hash samples do not justify runtime ranking.
Before/after source reads are not atomic, do not attest loaded code or dependencies, and miss transient changes restored between reads.
No target latency, jitter, hard real-time, MLS/CNSA or availability qualification. Insufficient information for tactical deployment.
